title: Patch: web and e2e tests turn the automatic turn end off instead of pinning seeds that deal a turn-one play
thread:
**Issue #2569 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #2569: Patch: web and e2e tests turn the automatic turn end off instead of pinning seeds that deal a turn-one play
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Several of the web client's tests need a game's first turn to stay open long enough to look at it. The game ends a turn by itself when the player has nothing to play, so these tests use a hand-picked game seed that happens to deal a playable card. Each time cards change, the deals change and these tests fail for no real reason. Whoever made the card change then has to hunt for a new seed: one test's comment lists five such moves, another file's lists seven. After this change, the tests turn the automatic turn end off, as one end-to-end test already does, or find a fitting seed by themselves. A card change then stops breaking them.

## Why
- Pinned seeds and their histories:
  - `apps/web/src/practice/core.test.ts:590-597`: R265's seeds moved for R186, twice for v0.1.1, and for #2278, #2454 and #2521.
  - `apps/web/src/game/hotseat.test.ts:569-570`: re-pinned for v0.3.5 and for v0.3.10.
  - `e2e/cypress/e2e/06-room-code.cy.ts:134-135`: re-pinned for R2368000's three-card opener.
  - `apps/web/src/test/replay.ts:14-31`: seven re-pins of one seed.
- R345: `setAutoEndTurn {enabled}` "is accepted from either seat at any moment of a live game, the mulligans and an open prompt included; it emits nothing".
- Commit `5aaf4f39c` (#2554) already fixed `e2e/cypress/e2e/20-mulligan-concede-draw.cy.ts` this way: "The browser turns R82's automatic turn end off (R345), so turn 1 stays open whatever the seed deals it".
- The Rust tests have a seed search (`crates/engine/src/testkit/seed_search.rs`, `seed_where`). The web tests have none.

## Proposal
- Where a test pins a seed only so a human seat's turn 1 holds a play, turn that seat's automatic turn end off before the mulligan ends (the setting in the browser, the action in the driver), and give the seed a fixed name.
- Where the seat is the AI's, or the test needs a property of the whole game (the hands at the end in `replay.ts`), add `seedWhere(prefix, accept)` in `apps/web/src/test/`, with its bound a named constant, mirroring the Rust `seed_where`.
- Drop the re-pin histories from the comments these changes make moot.

## Where it lands
`apps/web/src/practice/core.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/game/hotseat.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/test/replay.ts` with a new helper beside it, `e2e/cypress/e2e/06-room-code.cy.ts`, and any other test whose comment says it was re-pinned because R82 ended a turn (grep for "Re-pinned").

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No web or e2e test names a seed whose only purpose is a turn-one play.
- [ ] Each converted test still asserts what it did. For example, the R265 tests still prove the AI answers its mulligan first and the human's picker stays open.
- [ ] `seedWhere` fails with a message naming its prefix and bound when no seed fits.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test` and the touched Cypress specs pass.

## Size and risks
Small: about five test files, no rules change. A test that is about the automatic turn end itself (R82's, R345's) keeps it on. A search at run time costs a little time each run, so its bound stays small and its accept check cheap.
```
